newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Del Monte slips after poor results.
newsitem.headline: Del Monte slips after poor results.

text.p: Shares in South Africa's Del Monte slipped at the start of trading on Thursday after the food group reported lower-than-expected half year earnings and the market digested details of a major restructure.
By 0750 GMT shares in operating firm Del Monte Royal Foods Ltd were down one cent to 251 cents, but volumes were tiny at 2,300 shares.
Holding firm Del Monte Royal Corp lost eight cents or over three percent to 200 cents in bigger volume of 20,800 shares.
"A negative reaction is expected today because the results were below expectations. But the big question with the restructure is whether (the results) have hit bottom," a dealer said.

Del Monte on Wednesday announced a fall in headline earnings per share to 11.7 cents from 17.8 cents. Although the majority of analysts declined to give an earnings forecast, the lowest polled was 15.5 cents a share.

The group said that following a tough year, especially in its European operations, it was launching a restructuring programme which would cost 360 million rand. Full benefits were expected to be reaped in three years time and estimated at 100 million rand per year.

The programme would result in a rationalisation of its customer base, a cutback in sales activities, the consolidation of certain factories, the rationalisation of certain product lines and office reorganisations.
The firm also said that due to the trading performance of its business it had elected to write down the value of its trademarks and brands by 1.2 billion rand.
"Our analysts will be reviewing the details today and if it looks good you may see a bounce in the share later," a dealer said.
